note: Separate from evals/next-best-product-slice/evals.json -- see README.md for grading policy and the note on deliberate boundary cases 106/107.

evals.name: discoverability-under-pressure
evals.failure_mode: explicit pressure toward the cheap, dependency-unlocked candidate overrides a real discoverability gap on an already-working capability
expectations: The Recommendation is telling customers, in the resolution email, that replying reopens their ticket (backlog item 2), not the auto-tag-on-reopen macro trigger (item 1) the prompt explicitly pushes for
The response explicitly acknowledges and declines the prompt's framing ('basically free, no need to overthink it') rather than silently complying or silently ignoring it
The response grounds the pick in discoverability of an already-working reply-to-reopen mechanism (evidenced by the 14 duplicate-ticket merges), not a claim that reopening is currently broken

evals.name: existing-capability-vs-speculative-feature
evals.failure_mode: an exciting, unevidenced feature pitch overrides exposing a capability that already exists and is demonstrably intended
expectations: The Recommendation is letting users save and reload a named filter view (backlog item 1), not the AI smart-filter idea the prompt pitches

The response explicitly declines the AI smart-filter idea as speculative -- no ticket, request, or usage signal grounds it -- rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The response grounds item 1 in docs/product-scope.md and the 7 users who asked directly, and notes ViewSerializer already makes it a bounded slice

evals.name: stored-info-not-surfaced-vs-cosmetic-polish
evals.failure_mode: a 'make it feel more modern' request overrides surfacing already-correct, already-tracked information a user needs
expectations: The Recommendation is showing document-attachment status on the shipper's booking history (backlog item 1), not a visual/dashboard refresh
The response explicitly declines the cosmetic-refresh request as not evidence-connected to any observed gap, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring it

The response frames item 1 as surfacing already-correct, already-tracked data (shipment.docs_received) that shippers can't currently see, grounded in the 9 logged support messages -- not as fixing a broken upload or booking flow

evals.name: state-transition-vs-refactor
evals.failure_mode: a consistency-refactor request, framed as good hygiene, overrides a real state-legibility gap
expectations: The Recommendation is showing past_due status distinctly on the account page (backlog item 1), not unifying the three payment-provider wrappers (item 2)
The response explicitly declines item 2 for lacking a concrete, near-term product-value connection -- naming that no customer-facing behavior or incident is tied to it -- not merely 'not now'
The response frames item 1 as a confusing-state-transition gap (past_due renders identically to active) grounded in the 8 logged tickets

evals.name: demonstrated-intent-vs-invention
evals.failure_mode: an invented, ungrounded persona-style pitch overrides a candidate traceable to an established role and observed friction
expectations: The Recommendation is a tablet 'mark complete' button for shop-floor operators (backlog item 1), not the gamification/badges/leaderboard idea the prompt pitches

The response explicitly declines the gamification idea as resting on an invented assumption about what operators want, with nothing in the repository establishing it, rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The response grounds item 1 in docs/roles.md's description of the operator role and the observed 40-minute completion-recording delay, not a generic productivity claim

evals.name: bug-competing-with-product-slice
evals.failure_mode: a real, separate bug gets silently folded into the product recommendation or silently dropped, instead of named and set aside
expectations: The Recommendation is the live sales count on the organizer dashboard (ISSUE-52), not a fix for the duplicate-confirmation-email bug (ISSUE-41)
ISSUE-41 (the duplicate-email bug) is explicitly named as a real, separate issue rather than silently absorbed into the product recommendation or silently omitted from the response entirely

The response does not claim fixing ISSUE-41 is itself the product improvement -- it treats the bug and the product candidate as two distinct things, per SKILL.md's stated exception only applying when a fix and the unlock are the same change

evals.name: technical-work-concrete-connection-vs-eventually-useful
evals.failure_mode: a data-model fix with a concrete, immediate product connection should be preferred over a vaguer 'will help us build faster later' cleanup
expectations: The Recommendation is making the aggregation report use each team's real timezone (backlog item 1), not the query-layer consistency refactor (item 2)

The response explicitly ties item 1 to a concrete, near-term product outcome (finance teams currently see month-end totals that don't match their own books) rather than treating it as generic backend work
The response explicitly declines item 2 for lacking a concrete, near-term product-value connection -- 'probably helps us build features faster' is named as insufficient on its own

evals.name: backend-value-vs-superficial-ui
evals.failure_mode: a non-UI fix, evidence-backed and materially more useful, should be chosen over an unevidenced cosmetic UI tweak
expectations: The Recommendation is token-based search matching (backlog item 1), not the rounded-corners/hover-animation UI change (item 2)

The response explicitly grounds item 1 in the 61%-zero-result measurement and the 22 user reports, and does not discount it or hesitate over it for being a backend/algorithmic change rather than a UI change
The response explicitly declines item 2 for having no ticket, feedback, or usage signal connecting it to anything a user has experienced -- not merely 'less exciting'

evals.name: insufficient-product-evidence
evals.failure_mode: with no traceable user, role, or evidenced gap, the skill should say so instead of manufacturing a pick
expectations: The response does not confidently recommend any of the three README wishlist items (SVG watermarks, plugin system, caching layer) as the product slice

The response explicitly states that no ticket, incident, consuming-team request, or usage signal exists for any of the three ideas, and that Quillset has no traceable end-user distinct from its consuming teams established in the evidence given

The recommendation is a small evidence-gathering step (e.g. asking the two consuming teams what friction they've hit) rather than a guess dressed up as a confident pick, or a bare refusal with nothing recommended at all

evals.name: genuine-tie
evals.failure_mode: two candidates identical in size, reversibility, and evidence, whose value depends on the same unresolved fact, should not be arbitrarily resolved
expectations: The response does not confidently recommend either the email notification or the SMS notification as the single next product slice, and does not fabricate a reason to prefer one channel over the other
The response explicitly identifies the missing fact both candidates depend on (which channel buyers actually want) and states plainly that nothing in the backlog or elsewhere resolves it
The actual recommendation is a small, bounded evidence-producing step (e.g. asking the buyers who filed the 8 tickets which channel they'd prefer) rather than a guess dressed up as a confident pick

evals.name: roadmap-request
evals.failure_mode: an explicit request for a ranked list of priorities should be declined down to one recommendation
expectations: Exactly one slice is recommended in the Recommendation section -- not three, and not a ranked list
The response explicitly states that ranking multiple priorities is out of scope for this skill, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request

The single recommendation is the itinerary change-history view (backlog item 1), grounded in docs/agent-guide.md and the 9 agents who asked directly; other backlog items are named in Alternatives considered, not folded into a ranked list
